newsitem.title: DUBAI: Embassies to receive non-Saudi crew victims.
newsitem.headline: Embassies to receive non-Saudi crew victims.

text.p: Saudi Arabia was working with embassies to hand over the remains of non-Saudi crew members killed in a mid-air collision over India involving a Saudi jumbo jet, the official Saudi Press Agency (SPA) reported.
"We are working with embasssies and relatives of non-Saudi crew members to hand over their bodies," SPA quoted Saudi Arabian Airlines Corp director-general Khaled Ben-Bakr as saying on Friday night.
SPA earlier said the remains of 14 crew members and one Saudi passenger arrived in Saudi Arabia on Friday on a special flight from New Delhi bound for Jeddah.
The remains of the crew members include those of two Moroccans, a Jordanian, an Algerian, a Tunisian and nine Saudis, it added.

A Saudi Arabian Airlines jumbo jet with 312 people on board and a KazAir Ilyushin IL-76 freighter carrying 37 collided in flight on Tuesday, seven minutes after the Saudi plane had taken off from New Delhi. There were no survivors.
Officials earlier said there were 289 passengers on the Saudi flight -- 230 Indians, 51 Nepalese, three Pakistanis, two Americans, one Briton, one Bangladeshi and one Saudi national.
